title: 第十一节论偶然性的或然性

content.value:
但是，为了赋予这个体系以充分的力量和明显性，我们必须将我们的目光暂时离开这个体系，而要去考察体系的各种结论，
并且根据相同的原理去解释产生于同一根源的其他几种推理。
那些已经将人类理性分为知识和或然性，并且将知识定义为产生于观念之间的比较的那种证据的哲学家，他们都被迫将我们根据原因或结果而作的所有论证都包含在或然性这个基本术语之下。尽管每一个人都可以自由地根据他所乐意的意义去应用他的术语，并且在本书的前一个部分，我已经采取了这种表达方法，但是，在通常的谈论中，我们的确可以欣然地断言，由因果关系而来的许多论证都超过了或然性，并且可以被看作是一种较好的证明。如果一个人说太阳明天会升起或者所有的人都要死仅一253一

wou′ d say, that′tis only probable the sun will rise to-morrow, or that
all men must dye; tho''tis plain we have no further assurance of
these facts, than what experience affords us. For this reason,' twould
perhaps be more convenient, in order at once to preserve the common
signification of words, and mark the several degrees of evidence, to
distinguish human reason into three kinds, viz. that from knowledge,
from proofs,and from probabilities.By knowledge，I mean the assur-
ance arising from the comparison of ideas. By proofs, those argu-
ments, which are deriv' d from the relation of cause and effct, and
which are entirely free from doubt and uncertainty. By probability,
that evidence, which is still attended with uncertainty. ‘Tis this last
species of reasoning, I proceed to examine.
Probability or reasoning from conjecture may be divided into two
kinds, viz. that which is founded on chance, and that which arises
from causes. We shall consider each of these in order.
The idea of cause and effect is deriv′ d from experience, which
presenting us with certain objects constantly conjoin′d with each oth-
er, produces such a habit of surveying them in that relation, that we
cannot without a sensible violence survey them in any other. On the
other hand, as chance is nothing real in itself, and, properly speak-
ing, is merely the negation of a cause, its influence on the mind is
contrary to that of causation; and'tis essential to it, to leave the i-
magination perfectly indifferent, either to consider the existence or
non-existence of that object，which is regarded as contingent. A
cause traces the way to our thought, and in a manner forces us to sur-
vey such certaini objects, in such certain relations. Chance can only
destroy this determination of the thought, and leave the mind in its n-
ative situation of indifference; in which，upon the absence of a
cause, ' tis instantly re-instated.
Since therefore an entire indifference is essential to chance,
no one chance can possibly be superior to another, otherwise than

仅是可能的，那将是很可笑的事情；虽然除了经验能够提供给我们的以外，我们显然对这些事实没有更进一步的确信。由于这个原因，为了马上保存这些词的通常含义，并且标示出不同程度的证据，将人类的理性区分为三种也许更为方使。这三种就是根据知识的理性（推理）、根据证明的理性（推理）、根据或然性的理性
（推理）。所谓知识，我意指的是通过观念之间的比较而产生的确信。所谓证明，就是指源自于因果关系、并且完全没有怀疑和不确定的那些论证。所谓或然性，指的是仍然伴随有不确定的那种证据。而我现在要考察的就是最后这种推理。
或然性或者推测性的推理可以分为两种，也即建立在偶然性上的推理和产生于原因的推理。我们将依次对这两种推理加以研究。
因果观念乃是源自于经验，经验将某些彼此恒常结合的对象呈现给我们，因此就产生了在那种关系下观察它们的那种习惯，
以至我们在任何其他关系下都不能对它们进行强有力的观察。
另一方面，由于偶然性不是任何实在的东西，确切地说，它仅仅是某种原因的否定，因此它对心灵的影响就同因果关系对心灵的影响相反；对偶然性而言，其实质就是要使想象在考虑那个被看作是可能发生的对象的存在或不存在的时候，保持完全的中立。一个原因进人我们的思想，并且以某种方式强迫我们去观察某些关系下的某些对象。偶然性却只能破坏思想的这种决心，而使心灵保持本来冷静的中立情形；当原因不在场的时候，心灵的这种中立情形就会立刻重新就位。
因此，既然一个完全的中立对偶然性而言是必要的，那么除非一个偶然性包含有更大的同等偶然性，否则它就不可能优越于一255一

as it is compos’d of a superior number of equal chances.For if we af-
firm that one chance can, after any other manner, be superior to an-
other, we must at the same time affirm, that there is something,
which gives it the superiority, and determines the event rather to that
side than the other: That is, in other words, we must allow of a
cause, and destroy the supposition of chance; which we had before
establish’d. A perfect and total indifference is essential to chance,
and one total indifference can never in itself be either superior or infe-
rior to another. This truth is not peculiar to my system, but is ac-
knowledg’d by every one， that forms calculations concerming
chances.
And here′tis remarkable, that tho’ chance and causation be di-
rectly contrary, yet’tis impossible for us to conceive this combination
of chances, which is requisite to render one hazard superior to anoth-
er, without supposing a mixture of causes among the chances, and a
coujunction of necessity in some particulars, with a total indifference
in others. Where nothing limits the chances, every notion, that the
most extravagant fancy can form, is upon a footing of equality; nor
can there be any circumstance to give one the advantage above anoth-
er. Thus unless we allow, that there are some causes to make the dice
fall, and preserve their form in their fall, and lie upon some one of
their sides, we can form no calculation conceming the laws of hazard.
But supposing these causes to operate, and supposing likewise all the
rest to be indifferent and to be determin' d by chance, 'tis easy to ar-
rive at a notion of a superior combination of chances.A dye, that has
four sides mark ′ d with a certain number of spots, and only two with
another, affords us an obvious and easy instance of this superiority.
The mind is here limited by the causes to such a precise number and
quality of the events; and at the same time is undetermin′ d in its
choice of any particular event.
一256一

另一个偶然性。因为要是我肯定地说：一-个偶然性在任何其他方式下都优越于另一个偶然性，我们就必须在同时也肯定地说：存在着某种东西，它能给予那个偶然性优越性，并且决定其结果偏于那一面，而不是另一面。换句话说，也即我们必须承认一个原因，并且取消我们前面已经建立的那个偶然性的假定。对偶然性而言，一个完全的和全部的中立是必需的，并且一个全部的中立自身决不可能比另一个全部的中立更优越或更低劣。这种真理并不是我的体系所独有的，而是被每个计算过偶然性的人所承认。
在这里，值得注意的是：尽管偶然性和因果关系是直接相反的，但是对我们而言，如果不假定在那些偶然性中混杂有某些原因，以及在某些情况下必然性和另一些情况下全部中立性之间的结合，就不可能去构想对导致一个曾险比另一个冒险更优越而言是必需的各种偶然性的联结。如果没有什么对偶然性加以限制，
即使是由最过分的幻想形成的每个概念也能处于同等的地位；而且也没有任何情况能使一个概念优越于另一个概念。因此，除非我们承认，有某种原因导致了般子的下落，并使骰子在下落的过程中保持其形状，而且落到某一面上，否则我们就不能计算出冒险的几率。但是，如果假定这些原因发生作用，并且假定其他所有的原因都同样保持中立，而为偶然性所决定，那么就很容易获取一个各种偶然性的优势联结的概念。如果一个般子四个面都标记有某种点数，仅仅有两个面标记有另一种点数，那么它将给予我们一个关于这种优越性的明显和易懂的例子。在这里，心灵被原因限制于这些结果的非常精确的数目和性质，而且同时没有被决定选择其中任何一个特殊的结果。
—257一

Proceeding then in that reasoning, where in we have advanc′ d
three steps; that chance is merely the negation of a cause, and pro-
duces a total indifference in the mind; that one negation of a cause
and one total indifference can never be superior or inferior to another;
and that there must always be a mixture of causes among the chances,
in order to be the foundation of any reasoning: We are next to consid-
er what effect a superior combination of chances can have upon the
mind , and after what manner it influences our judgment and opinion.
Here we may repeat all the same arguments we employ ′ d in exami-
ning that belief, which arises from causes; and may prove after the
same manner, that a superior number of chances produces our assent
neither by demonstration nor probability. ’Tis indeed evident, that we
can never by the comparison of mere ideas make any discovery, which
can be of consequence in this affair, and that’ tis impossible to prove
with certainty, that any event must fall on that side where there is a
superior number of chances. To suppose in this case any certainty,
were to overthrow what we have establish′ d concerming the opposition
of chances, and their perfect equality and indifference.
Shou' d it be said, that tho′in an opposition of chances′ tis im-
possible to determine with certainty, on which side the event will fall,
yet we can pronounce with certainty, that’ tis more likely and proba-
ble,'twill be on that side where there is a superior number of
chances, than where there is an inferior: shou' d this be said, I wou′ d
ask, what is here meant by likelihood and probability? The likelihood
and probability of chances is a superior number of equal chances; and
consequently when we say' tis likely the event will fall on the side,
which is superior, rather than on the inferior, we do no more than af-
firm, that where there is a superior number of chances there is actually
a superior, and where there is an inferior there is an inferior; which
are identical propositions, and of no consequence. The question is, by
what means a superior number of equal chances operates upon the mind,
一258—

于是，我们已经将上面的推理推进了三步：即偶然性仅仅是原因的否定，它在心灵中产生了一个完全的中立；一个原因的否定和一个完全的中立决不能比另一个原因的否定和另一个完全的中立更为优越或低劣；为了构成任何推理的基础，偶然性中必定总是掺杂有一些原因。下面我们就要考察各种偶然性的优势联结对心灵有什么作用，以及它在随后是以什么方式来影响我们的判断和意见的。在这里，我们可以重复我们在考察根据原因而产生的信念时所应用的全部论证，并且可以随后以同样的方式证明，之所以更大的偶然性会产生我们的同意，既不是因为实证，也不是因为或然性。显而易见，我们确实永远不能通过单纯观念之间的比较就有在这件事情上的任何重大的发现，而且我们也不能确定地证明，任何结果都必定会指向有更大的偶然性的那一边。
在这种情况下，如果假定有任何确定性，那将会推翻我们已经建立的关于各种偶然性的相互对立，以及它们都是完全相等和中立的那个原则。
如果有人将会说，在偶然性相互对立的情形下，虽然我们不可能确定地决定结果将会落在那一边，但是我们可以确定地断言，它大约和很可能会落在有更大的偶然性那一边，而不是落在有更小的偶然性那一边。如果有人这样说，我就要问，“大约”和
“很可能”在这里指的是什么意思呢？大约的和很可能的偶然性是更大的同等偶然性，因此，当我们说，结果大约会落在更大的偶然性那一边而不是落在更小的偶然性那一边时，我们只是断言，
在更大偶然性那一边，实际上有一个优势，而在更小偶然性那一边，实际上有一个劣势；这乃是在说一些相同的命题，本身并不是重要的。问题在于：多数的同等偶然性以什么方式作用于心灵，
一259一

and produces belief or assent; since it appears, that′tis neither by ar-
guments deriv' d from demonstration, nor from probability.
In order to clear up this dificulty, we shall suppose a person to
take a dye, form' d after such a manner as that four of its sides are
mark′ d with one figure, or one number of spots, and two with anoth-
er; and to put this dye into the box with an intention of throwing it :
'Tis plain, he must conclude the one figure to be more probable than
the other, and give the preference to that which is inscrib’ d on the
greatestnumber of sides. He in a manner believes, that this will lie
uppermost; tho’still with hesitation and doubt, in proportion to the
number of chances, which are contrary : And according as these con-
trary chances diminish, and the superiority encreases on the other
side, his belief acquires new degrees of stability and assurance. This
belief arises from an operation of the mind upon the simple and limit-
ed object before us; and therefore its nature will be the more easily
discover'd and explain' d. We have nothing but one single dye to
contemplate, in order to comprehend one of the most curious opera-
tions of the understanding.
This dye form’d as above, contains three circumstances worthy
of our attention.First, Certain causes, such as gravity,solidity,a cu
bical figure, &c. which determine it to fall, to preserve its form in its
fall, and to turm up one of its sides. Secondly, A certain number of
sides, which are suppos′ d indifferent. Thirdly, A certain figure, in-
scrib′ d on each side. These three particulars form the whole nature of
the dye, so far as relates to our present purpose; and consequently
are the only circumstances regarded by the mind in its forming a judg-
ment concerning the result of such a throw. Let us, therefore, consid-
er gradually and carefully what must be the influence of these circum-
stances on the thought and imagination.
First, We have already observ' d, that the mind is determin’ d
by custom to pass from any cause to its effect, and that upon the
appearance of the one, ' tis almost impossible for it not to form
一260一

并且产生信念和赞同；因为它看起来既不是根据产生于实证的论证，也不是根据产生于或然性的论证。
为了澄清这一困难，我们可以假定一个人拿着一个般子，般子的四面被标记有一个图形或点数，其余两面则标记有另一个图形或点数；并且假定他将这个股子放在一个盒子里，准备去摇掷它。显然，他必然会断定前一个图形要比后一个图形出现的几率要大，这就使得他优先考虑去选择那个刻在更多面的那个图形。
在某种意义上，他相信这一面将会朝上，尽管他根据相反偶然性的数目，他对此仍会有一种跨曙和犹豫。而随着这些相反的偶然性的减少，以及另一面优越性的增加，他的信念就获取了新的可靠和确定程度。这一信念源自于心灵对我们前面的那个简单而有限的对象的作用，因此其本质将会更容易被发现和加以解释。
为了理解知性的最为神奇的一种作用，我们只要思考单单一个般子就行了。
根据上述方式做成的这个般子，包括了三种值得我们注意的情况。第一，一定的原因，例如重力、坚固性、方形等等。这些原因决定了般子的下落，使它在下落过程中保持其形状，并且使它一个面朝上。第二，被假定为没有差异的一定数目的面。第三，
刻在各个面的某一图形。就其关涉到我们当下的自的而言，这三种情况构成了般子的全部本质；因此，当心灵形成关于摇掷骰子的结果的判断时，上述三种情况就是它所考虑的唯一的情形。
所以，让我们依次和仔细地考察这些情况对思想和想象必然会受到什么影响。
首先，我们已经说过，心灵被习惯决定由任何原因推到它的结果，并且当其中任何一个出现时，心灵就几乎不可能不

an idea of the other. Their constant conjunction in past instances has
produe ′ d such a habit in the mind, that it always conjoins them in its
thought, and infers the existence of the one from that of its usual at-
tendant. When it considers the dye as no longer supported by the box,
it cannot without violence regard it as suspended in the air; but natu-
rally places it on the table, and views it as tuming up one of its sides.
This is the effect of the intermingled causes, which are requisite to
our forming any calculation concerning chances.
Secondly,'Tis suppos’d, that tho′the dye be necessarily de-
termin′ d to fall, and turn up one of its sides, yet there is nothing
to fix the particular side，but that this is determin'd entirely by
chance. The very nature and essence of chance is a negation of cau-
ses , and the leaving the mind in a perfect indifference among those
events，which are suppos′d contingent.When therefore the
thought is determin′ d by the causes to consider the dye as falling
and turning up one of its sides, the chances present all these sides
as equal, and make us consider every one of them, one after an-
other, as alike probable and possible. The imagination passes from
the cause， viz. the throwing of the dye, to the effect， viz. the
turning up one of the six sides; and feels a kind of impossibility
both of stopping short in the way, and of forming any other idea.
But as all these six sides are incompatible, and the dye cannot turn
up above one at once, this principle directs us not to consider all of
them at once as lying uppermost; which we look upon as impossi-
ble: Neither does it direct us with its entire force to any particular
side; for in that case this side wou' d be consider' d as certain and
inevitable; but it directs us to the whole six sides after such a man-
ner as to divide its force equally among them. We conclude in gen-
eral, that some one of them must result from the throw: We run all of
them over in our minds: The determination of the thought is common
to all; but no more of its force falls to the share of any one, than what
is suitable to its proportion with the rest. 'Tis after this manner the
—262—

去形成关于另一个的观念。原因和结果在过去的例子中的恒常结合已经在心灵中产生了这样一种习惯，以至它总是把原因和结果结合在它的思想中，并且由一个的存在推论出通常伴随着它的另一个的存在。当心灵考虑到般子不再为盒子支撑的时候，它就很难认为般子是悬在空中的，而是自然地考虑到它是在桌子上，
并且将它看作是一面朝上的。这就是我们形成任何偶然性的推算所必需的那些混合原因的结果。
其次，假定虽然子必然被决定要落下，并且一面朝上，可是却没有确定是一面朝上，而确定哪一面朝上完全取决于偶然性。偶然性的恰当本质和要素是对原因的否定，并且使心灵在那些假定为可能发生的结果中处于完全中立的状态。因此，当思想被原因决定着去考虑般子的下落以及有一面朝上的时候，偶然性就同样地呈现所有的这些面，并使我们考虑到这些面中的每一个都具有同样的或然性和可能性。想象由原因，也即掷般子，推论出结果，也即六个面中有一个面朝上；它感觉到，自己既不可能在半路上突然停止，也不可能形成任何其他的观念。但是，既然这六个面全都是不容调和的，而且般子不可能同时有一个以上的面朝上，所以这个原理就告诉我们不要把般子的六个面看成是同时朝上的，在我们着来这是不可能的事情。这个原理也不会以它的全部力量把我们引向任何特殊的一面；因为在那种情况下，这个特殊的面就会被看作是确定和必然的。但是根据那种方式，这个原理把我们引向了全部的六个面，以至使得它的力量平分于六个面。我们大体推断出，六个面中一定有某个面是因投掷而朝上的，我们在心中将它们一一思考，思想的决定对所有的面来说是共同的；不过它们中的任何一面都不会享有超过依其比例而分享的思

original impulse, and consequently the vivacity of thought, arising
from the causes, is divided and split in pieces by the intermingled
chances.
We have already seen the influence of the two first qualities of
the dyeiz.thecauses，and thenumber and indiffeencef the side
and have learm’ d how they give an impulse to the thought, and divide
that impulse into as many parts as there are unites in the number of
sides. We must now consider the effects of the third particular, viz.
the figures inscrib′ d on each side. 'Tis evident that where several
sides have the same figure inscrib’ d on them, they must concur in
their influence on the mind , and must unite upon one image or idea of
a figure all those divided impulses, that were dispers’ d over the sev-
eral sides, upon which that figure is inscrib’d. Were the question on-
ly what side will be tum′ d up, these are all perfectly equal, and no
one cou’ d ever have any advantage above another. But as the question
is concerming the figure, and as the same figure is presented by more
than one side;′ tis evident, that the impulses belonging to all these
sides must re-unite in that one figure, and become stronger and more
forcible by the union. Four sides are suppos’ d in the present case to
have the same figure inscrib′ d on them, and two to have another fig-
ure, The impulses of the former are, therefore, superior to those of
the latter. But as the events are contrary, and’ tis impossible both
these figures can be turn′ d up; the impulses likewise become contra-
ry, and the inferior destroys the superior, as far as its strength goes.
The vivacity of the idea is always proportionable to the degrees of the
impulse or tendency to the transition; and belief is the same with the
vivacity of the idea, according to the precedent doctrine.
SECTIONXII.OfTheProbabilityOfCauses.
What I have said concerning the probability of chances can
serve to no other purpose, than to assist us in explaining the proba-
bility of causes; since′tis commonly allow’ d by philosophers, that

想的力量。原初的冲动，以及因此而由原因产生的思想的活泼性，都按照这种方式而被混合的偶然性分裂成一些片断。
我们已经看到了股子的前两种性质的影响，也即原因和各个面的数目和中立性，并且知道它们是怎样给予思想以一种冲动，
以及怎样将冲动分成和面数的单位相等的许多部分。现在，我们必须考察第三个方面的作用，也即刻在各个面上的图形的作用。
显然，当几个面上已经刻有相同的图形的时候，这些面必定会同时对心灵产生影响，而且必定会把分散在刻有那个图形的几个面上的冲动集中到一个图形的意象或观念上。如果问题仅仅在于到底是哪一个面朝上，那么这些面就是完全相等的，没有一个面要比另一个面更占有优势。但是，既然问题在于图形，并且由于同一个图形又被不止一个面所皇现，那么显然，所有属于这些面的冲动都必定会重新结合在那个图形上，并且由于这种结合而变得更强壮，更有力。在目前这种情况下，我们假定同一个图形被刻在四个面上，而另一个图形被刻在两个面上。因此，前者的冲动就要比后者的冲动更为强烈。但是，既然结果都是相反的，并且这两个图形不可能同时朝上，所以冲动也同样地变得相反，而力量较小的一面也就尽其所能地摧毁力量更大的一面。观念的活泼性总是与那种冲动的程度或那种过渡的倾向成比例的；而根据前面的学说，信念与观念的活泼性乃是一样的。
